title: Air India Inflight Wi-Fi Goes Paid With Three Plans Starting at ₹299
excerpt: After 19 months of complimentary service, Air India now charges for onboard internet across economy, premium economy, and business class, with free access reserved for first class and top-tier loyalty members.
body:
• Air India's inflight Wi-Fi became a paid service on August 1, 2026, ending a 19-month free introductory period that began in January 2025.
  • Three plans are available: Chat (₹399 full flight), Basic Browsing (₹299 to ₹1,199), and Streaming (₹2,699 full flight).
  • First class passengers and Platinum Maharaja Club members retain unlimited free Wi-Fi; business class gets one hour of free browsing and full-flight chat.
  • The service runs on 28 Wi-Fi-enabled aircraft across the A350, B787-9, B777-300ER, and select A321neo fleet, covering over 55 daily flights.

The Free Ride Is Over

When Air India rolled out inflight Wi-Fi on January 1, 2025, it became the first Indian carrier to offer internet connectivity on domestic flights. The service was free — a move designed to build passenger loyalty as the Tata Group-owned airline overhauled its fleet and brand under a sweeping transformation plan.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=iv1p8Co1mjo

That complimentary period ended on August 1, 2026. Nineteen months after launch, Air India has transitioned inflight Wi-Fi to a paid model with three tiered plans, according to travel platform Indian Eagle.

What the Plans Cost

The pricing is structured around how passengers actually use in-flight internet:

Chat and Text — ₹399 for the full flight. Covers messaging apps like WhatsApp and basic text communication. This is the option for passengers who just need to stay reachable.

Basic Browsing — ₹299 for one hour, ₹699 for three hours, or ₹1,199 for the full flight. Supports email, social media, web browsing, and cloud-based services. The one-hour option makes it practical for short domestic hops.

Streaming — ₹2,699 for the full flight. Designed for passengers who want uninterrupted access to video and music streaming services throughout their journey. At roughly $32, it is priced at a premium but sits within the range of what carriers like Lufthansa and Emirates charge for comparable plans on long-haul routes.

Payments are made onboard after takeoff. Air India accepts UPI and international credit or debit cards that do not require OTP verification — a practical consideration for passengers already in the air.

"To connect, passengers activate airplane mode, select the "Air India Wi-Fi" network, and log in through a browser portal using their booking reference and surname."

Who Still Flies Free

Not everyone pays. First class passengers and Platinum-tier Maharaja Club members get unlimited Wi-Fi for the entire flight, including streaming. Business class passengers receive one hour of free browsing and full-flight chat access; after the free hour, they can purchase a browsing or streaming plan.

Lower tiers of the Maharaja Club loyalty programme get more limited benefits: Red and Silver members receive one hour of free chat access, while Gold members get one hour of browsing and full-flight chat.

Where It Works

Air India's Wi-Fi service is available on 28 aircraft: the Airbus A350-900, Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, select Boeing 777-300ER, and select Airbus A321neo planes. These aircraft operate more than 55 daily flights across the airline's domestic and international network, including nonstop routes to the US, UK, and major Asian hubs.

To connect, passengers activate airplane mode, select the "Air India Wi-Fi" network, and log in through a browser portal using their booking reference and surname. The service becomes available once the aircraft reaches cruising altitude.

In April 2026, Air India selected Hughes Network Systems to provide a unified connectivity platform across its widebody fleet, with a roadmap to upgrade to home-broadband-level speeds within two years using a combination of geostationary and low-earth orbit satellite networks.

How It Compares

Air India's move to paid Wi-Fi goes against the global trend. Several major carriers — including JetBlue, Air New Zealand, United Airlines, and Delta — now offer free onboard internet, some through Starlink partnerships. Air France rolled out free Wi-Fi for loyalty members in late 2024, and American Airlines followed in early 2026.

Among Indian carriers, Air India remains the only one offering inflight internet on domestic routes, giving it a differentiation advantage even with the new charges. IndiGo, which is expanding aggressively into long-haul with its A350 fleet, has not yet announced inflight Wi-Fi plans.

For frequent flyers on the India-US corridor, the practical calculus is straightforward: the ₹1,199 full-flight browsing plan on a 15-hour flight to New York works out to about ₹80 per hour — less than most airport lounge Wi-Fi day passes.
nri_angle: NRIs flying the India-US corridor will now pay for a service that was previously complimentary, though the pricing remains competitive for long-haul flights.
